affectedPublicSurfaces: THE APPROVE REQUEST BODY. `api/routes/demo_execution.py::approve_demo_decision` (`POST /v1/demo/decisions/{action_card_id}/approve`) today takes NO request body at all — its signature is `(action_card_id, shop=Depends(...), user=Depends(...), session=Depends(...))`. It gains an OPTIONAL typed body: a small map of seller inputs, VALIDATED PER WORKFLOW against what that workflow declares. Backward compatible by construction — an absent body and an empty body must both behave exactly as today, which is the post-deploy assertion. An undeclared key is REFUSED, not ignored; silently dropping a value the seller typed is the failure mode this slice exists to prevent.

THE CONFIRMATION DECIDE BODY. `api/routes/agent_runs.py::submit_confirmation_decision` (`POST /v1/demo/runs/{run_id}/confirmations/{tool_call_id}`) today accepts `ConfirmationDecisionRequest {decision, option_id}`. For the new `report` kind it gains a `values` map. The single-option shape (N = 1, S-FR-3) is UNCHANGED for every tool that exists today, asserted against a golden.

`run_confirmations` GAINS A `kind` COLUMN — and the executor must know what is and is not there today. `models.py::RunConfirmation` (migration 039) has exactly `id`, `workflow_run_id`, `tool_call_id`, `options` (JSON), `status`, `selected_option_id`, `created_at`, `decided_at`, `expires_at`. There is NO `kind` column, and — important — THERE IS NO `params_sha` COLUMN EITHER: the hash lives inside each `options[]` entry in the JSON blob. Do not go looking for a column to change; the hash's home is the option entry.

THE DIRECTION OF THE CONSENT HASH INVERTS, and this is the substance of the slice. `services/agent_runs/confirmations.py` computes `expected_params_sha = compute_params_sha(pending_state["arguments"])` — the MODEL's own stored tool-call arguments — and rejects a mismatch with `ERROR_PARAMS_SHA_MISMATCH` (`compute_params_sha` itself lives in `services/agent/runner/confirmation.py`: a SHA-256 hex digest over the canonicalised params). For a `report` kind the hash must instead cover THE SELLER-SUPPLIED VALUES AT DECIDE TIME, because those values do not exist when the run creates the confirmation. Today NO path exists where params are seller-supplied — the only seller-supplied value anywhere in a run is `pending_image_bytes`, a staged FILE in run context. This inversion touches ADR-075's consent binding and must be built as a NEW kind beside the existing one, never by loosening the existing check.

RUN STATE AND THE APPROVAL AUDIT. Seller inputs live in run state (the `state` JSON on `workflow_runs`) and are included in the card-snapshot audit that `approval.py` captures BEFORE it flips `card.status` to 'approved' — so the audit records what was shown AND what the seller typed. `action_card_approvals` is already tenant-scoped under RLS; the snapshot's shape widens, its tenancy does not.
NOT IN SCOPE, though the wire allows it: the FORM UI. W9-D builds it. This slice makes the values expressible and binding; nothing renders them.

migrationCompatibility.notes: ONE ADDITIVE, EXPAND-ONLY migration adding a NULLABLE `kind` column to `run_confirmations` (migration 039's table). No column is dropped, renamed or retyped; no backfill; no NOT NULL. Existing rows keep NULL, which must READ as the pre-existing single-option kind — decide that default explicitly in code, because a NULL that silently becomes 'report' would let the seller-value hashing path run over a model-argument confirmation. Note what is NOT being added: `params_sha` is NOT and does not become a column — it lives inside each `options[]` entry in the existing JSON blob, and this slice keeps it there. Old and new code coexist: the previous release neither writes nor reads `kind`, and every confirmation it creates is the single-option shape it already understands. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Approve keeps taking no body, the params hash keeps covering only the model's stored tool arguments, no confirmation kind exists where the seller supplies the values, and Clear Excess's stock goal and Replenish's received report stay unexpressible. That is the pre-existing state; nothing is exposed and nothing is partially applied.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release FIRST and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker: the previous code neither reads nor writes `kind` and rejects an unexpected request body the way FastAPI already rejects one, so it runs correctly with the column present and needs NO downgrade. Stored seller inputs are INERT to it — a `state` blob key it never reads. THE ONE REAL HAZARD, to state in the PR and assert pre-merge: a `report` confirmation created on the candidate and still PENDING when the rollback lands cannot be decided by the previous release, because its hash covers values the previous decide path never collects. It must fail CLOSED with the existing named error and expire on its own 4 h timer — never execute with the model's arguments substituted, which would be an unconsented write. Only if the schema must also be reverted, `alembic downgrade -1` drops `kind`, and that downgrade MUST FAIL LOUDLY when any `run_confirmations` row carries a non-default `kind` in a non-terminal status (and, when #1701's or #1706's schema is being reverted in the same operation, on any non-product `subject_type`, NULL `product_id`, or `waiting_external` row). Order: previous code first, downgrade second.

doNotInfer: The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake. This slice DOES carry a migration (`run_confirmations.kind`), so the reservation is binding, not advisory.

Do NOT hash the model's arguments for a report confirmation. `compute_params_sha(pending_state["arguments"])` is the EXISTING binding for the existing kind and must keep working exactly as it does. A `report` hashes THE SELLER-SUPPLIED VALUES AT DECIDE TIME — that inversion is the point of the slice. Hashing the model's arguments and calling it a report would bind consent to a number the seller never typed.

Do NOT loosen the existing consent check to accommodate the new kind. `ERROR_PARAMS_SHA_MISMATCH` and `confirmation_diverged` (produced only by `runner/core.py::resume`'s consent check) stay exactly as they are; the report kind is a NEW branch beside them, never a relaxation of them.

Do NOT look for a `params_sha` column — there isn't one, and do not add one. The hash lives inside each `options[]` entry in `run_confirmations.options`. Adding a column would create a second place for the same fact.

Do NOT let a NULL `kind` mean 'report'. Existing rows have NULL and are the pre-existing single-option kind; decide that default explicitly in code so a historical confirmation can never be routed through the seller-value path.

Do NOT mutate a decided report. A corrected value is a NEW report row; rewriting the decided one would rewrite consent that has already been given, and the audit would no longer show what the seller actually saw.
Do NOT allow a report to be decided twice. Single-use must hold under concurrency inside the transaction, not as a status read followed by a write.

Do NOT change the single-option shape (N = 1, S-FR-3) for any existing tool, and do NOT change the 4 h confirmation expiry or the 5/h burst-2 approval rate limit (S-NFR-2). ZERO behaviour change for `optimize_product_2` — the golden `tests/fixtures/golden_scenarios/optimize_product_confirm_pause.json` is a confirm-pause scenario and must pass UNREGENERATED.
Do NOT build the form UI. W9-D renders it; this slice only makes the values expressible and binding. A route that returns render instructions is out of scope.
Do NOT silently ignore an undeclared key in the approve body. Refuse it. A dropped value the seller typed is exactly the class of defect this wave exists to eliminate.

Do NOT derive the subject from revenue, do NOT emit a per-order card, and do NOT reuse the emission-budget suppression vocabulary (`active_cap`/`cooldown`/`weekly_novelty_cap`) — none of it belongs on a consent path.
Do NOT add a second reaper policy object, and do NOT add a push, email or Zalo transport. A pending report notifies nobody in this slice; the in-app act record is #1712/#1713.
Do NOT gate anything on a checklist tick — checklist items exist in #1712/#1713 and never gate a stage in v1 (S-FR-12).
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/** — this epic's doNotLoad list.

Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature — the real routes through the real app, the real `compute_params_sha`, the real tool through the real registry. A `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the real call would work.
